title: Global Fusion Explorer
description: An interactive world map of 60 fusion facilities and the activity From Competition to Collaboration: how the geography of fusion research changed from Cold War secrecy to worldwide networks.

sources.title: Course data: Global Fusion Explorer facilities (assets/units/fy14/data/facilities.json, each facility with its own sources)
sources.note: 60 facilities, data checked 2026-11-01. Counts in this unit were computed from this file: before 1970 machines in three countries; facilities with status 'operating' in 12 countries.

sources.title: UN Digital Library: Second United Nations International Conference on the Peaceful Uses of Atomic Energy, Geneva, 1–13 September 1958
Timeline of nuclear fusion (Wikipedia): declassification in 1958, T-3 results 1968–1969
UKAEA: Mission to Moscow, 50 years on (the 1969 Culham measurement of T-3)
Tokamak (Wikipedia): T-3 and the spread of tokamaks after 1969
EUR-Lex: Council Decision 78/471/Euratom of 30 May 1978 on the establishment of the Joint European Torus (JET) Joint Undertaking
ITER (Wikipedia): origins at the 1985 Geneva summit, the ITER Agreement of 21 November 2006 and its seven members
HL-2A (Wikipedia): built from the main parts of the German ASDEX tokamak
COMPASS tokamak (Wikipedia): from Culham to the Institute of Plasma Physics in Prague
JT-60SA (Wikipedia): joint project of Japan and the European Union, first plasma on 23 October 2023
OpenStreetMap: copyright and licence of the map tiles
sources.note: Map tiles © OpenStreetMap contributors; loaded by the student's browser, so the map needs an internet connection.
